Three ants walk on a thin rod 100 cm long.
When an ant reaches either end of the rod it falls off. When two ants meet,
they BOUNCE: both instantly reverse direction, and each keeps its own speed.

Starting positions and velocities (positive = toward the 100 cm end):

- Ant A: at 10 cm, moving +3 cm/s
- Ant B: at 40 cm, moving -1 cm/s
- Ant C: at 80 cm, moving -2 cm/s

After how many seconds does the LAST ant fall off the rod? Give the exact
number of seconds.


When you are finished, output your final answer on its own line, as the last line of your response, in the exact format:
ANSWER: <your answer>

text:
First, A and B meet:

\[
10+3t=40-t \implies t=\frac{15}{2}\text{ s}
\]

at position \(\frac{65}{2}\) cm. They reverse directions: A goes left at 3 cm/s, B goes right at 1 cm/s. C is then at 65 cm going left at 2 cm/s.

Next, B and C meet after

\[
\frac{65-\frac{65}{2}}{1+2}=\frac{65}{6}\text{ s}
\]

so the absolute time is

\[
\frac{15}{2}+\frac{65}{6}=\frac{55}{3}\text{ s}.
\]

At that same time, A falls off the left end. B and C bounce: B now moves left at 1 cm/s, C moves right at 2 cm/s. They are at \(\frac{130}{3}\) cm.

C falls off the right end after

\[
\frac{100-\frac{130}{3}}{2}=\frac{85}{3}\text{ s}.
\]

B falls off the left end after

\[
\frac{\frac{130}{3}}{1}=\frac{130}{3}\text{ s}.
\]

So B is last, falling at

\[
\frac{55}{3}+\frac{130}{3}=\frac{185}{3}\text{ s}.
\]

ANSWER: 185/3
